notes.title: Repair System - Fuse Replacement
notes.content:
Hey Car Dealers!

Only 3 days left until the release!

In today’s devlog, we’ve got another batch of info about the mechanical repair system. This time, we’re focusing on fuse replacement.

On the scanner report, you’ll notice a section labeled "Fuses." If the percentage shown is lower than 100%, it means that some fuses are either blown or missing.

Once you enter Repair Mode and click on the fuse box, you’ll see their condition - blown fuses or empty slots. Thanks to the highlight system, you’ll know exactly which fuse should go where.

Here’s how it works:

- To remove a fuse, just click on it.
- To insert a new one, click on the appropriate fuse on the right side, then confirm where you want to place it.

You can buy fuses in the shop or at the gas station, so it’s a good idea to always have a few in stock.

notes.title: Mechanical Repairs and How They Affect Value and Reputation
notes.content:
Hey Car Dealers!

Only 9 days left until the release of Car Dealer Simulator - the countdown to May 29, 2025 is on!

Today’s devlog kicks off a short series focused on mechanical repairs. Think of it as a mini guidebook to help you understand how to handle them effectively in the game.

Most cars in Car Dealer Simulator are purchased through the classifieds portal. Vehicles come in various conditions, and you can already check key info like visual state and whether the car starts or not directly in the listing.

But to get a detailed technical overview, you’ll need to use the diagnostic scanner.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/82df00ca73de833d37f3c50852148bcf77ab4a91.gif

Once used, the scanner will show you a full report on the condition of every part in the vehicle.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/2c170aaf0fb9bfa701f853d77b1271b9413e81f8.png

🔧 Pro tip: If you’re out shopping and forget what needed fixing - don’t worry. Just pull out the scanner from the radial menu and press ‘R’ to open the last saved report. Even better, the report updates automatically after every part replacement, so you’re always working with the latest info.

Every repair you make directly affects the market value of the vehicle - the more you fix, the more profit you can earn. And that’s not just about cash.

💼 Your dealer reputation depends on how much profit you make from each sale – the higher the difference between the purchase and sale price, the more reputation points you’ll gain. So smart repairs and good deals really pay off.

In the next entries, we’ll walk you through how to replace specific parts and what to keep an eye on.

See you in the workshop - on May 29, 2025!

notes.title: Employees at Workstations How Do They Work and What Can They Do?
notes.content:
Hey Car Dealers!

Only 16 days left until the release!

In today’s devlog, we’re continuing our series about room upgrades. One of the final upgrade levels for the workshop, car wash, and body shop introduces a big feature: the ability to hire an employee. The hiring process is handled through an app on your in-game computer – just open it and choose the person you want to hire.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/dbe3ba82fca03cef40c4e0e79a99a90435fa0337.gif

Once hired, the employee must be assigned to a workstation.
Important! - each employee has an hourly wage, and you’ll be charged for each hour they’re assigned to a workstation. The payment is settled once per day - as a single daily wage visible at the end of the day. Employees are not locked into specific roles, so you can freely reassign them between workstations as needed.

So how do you make an employee do some work?
It’s simple - just park a car in the area next to the employee’s workstation and interact with them.

In the car wash and body shop, things are straightforward - the employee will automatically perform all the necessary tasks.
In the workshop, however, you’ll need to specify exactly what you want done. A dialog window will show all the parts installed in the car - you can instruct the employee to remove them to your warehouse or replace them with another part from your inventory.

Once confirmed, the employee will begin their work sequence, and a progress bar above their head will show you how long the task will take.

notes.content:
Hello Car Dealers!

In today’s devlog, we’re going image-free, but we want to share some insights about our current work on the game. One of the key elements we’re currently reworking is the save system.

In the prologue, the gameplay was rather linear, so the save system mainly relied on checkpoints. However, in the demo, we are gradually opening up the game world to provide you with complete freedom in making decisions - what cars you buy, what you do with them, and how you manage your business.

Points of Interest (POIs) – key locations such as:

Gas Station – for refueling your vehicles.
Parts Shop – to stock up on tools and parts.
Workshop – your everyday workspace.

Tasks – icons representing missions you can take on, such as picking up a car from a client or delivering a vehicle to a specific location.

Map filtering

Dynamic route planning
Clicking on a marker automatically plots the shortest route to your destination. The GPS will guide you from your current location, showing the route on the map and the in-game HUD.

Tasks and POIs are visually differentiated, so you’ll always know if a marker represents a gas station, parts shop, workshop, or a mission you need to complete.

Hey, car dealers and aspiring mechanics! 🚗⛽

Today, we’re diving into a feature every dealership needs to master: refueling. Whether prepping a car for sale or making sure your latest acquisition runs smoothly, you’ll be spending some time at the pump. Let's take a closer look at how the refueling mechanic works in the Car Dealer Simulator and why it’s more than just topping off the tank!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/f7ec2c17e2ac7ffe231fd78e232859c6f63afb94.gif

Parking and Positioning: Fuel Up Like a Pro
First things first, when you roll up to the pump, it’s essential to get your car in the right spot. You’ll notice a visible zone next to the pump where your vehicle needs to be parked. Once you’re in position, the fun begins! With a click, you’ll grab the refueling gun, place it into the fuel filler, and get ready to refuel.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/bd0f0a3712b877c3734dbc7818a70e607b0318cf.gif

Fueling Options: Manual or Automatic – The Choice is Yours
Once the gun is in place, the refueling UI pops up, and you’ve got two options. You can either manually fill the tank by holding the LMB or switch on the Auto Fill feature to make things easier. Auto Fill lets you fill the tank without holding the button, allowing the fuel to flow until the tank is full—or your wallet runs dry!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/2db2b36a692c6b30012d20a07edbb0431461b3a3.gif

Once you’re done refueling, hit the button at the bottom of the UI to confirm your purchase. The game will notify you of the fuel added and the funds deducted from your account, so you’ll always know exactly where you stand. Seamless and Satisfying
The refueling mechanic is designed to feel as natural and smooth as possible, whether you prefer doing things manually or letting the Auto Fill handle it for you. Every refueling session becomes essential to maintaining your cars, getting them ready for the road, or primed for sale.

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/ede5fd984215365b633be07d802748f64d568319.png

Hey, car dealers and repair enthusiasts! 🚗🛠️

This week, we’re excited to take you through one of the fundamental mechanics in Car Dealer Simulator: Bodywork Restoration. If you’ve ever wanted to transform a rusty old car into something that gleams, this is your chance to dive into the nitty-gritty of what it takes to make that happen. Let’s walk through the process of bringing those neglected cars back to life, one fender at a time.

Rust Removal: Getting Hands-On

When you step into the workshop or the body repair pavilion, you’ll have complete control over repairing rusted sills and fenders. As soon as you start interacting with the vehicle, a tool selection HUD appears, giving you everything you need to start. Simply select the part you want to work on and get to work with the right tools for the job.
Whether sanding, applying putty, or polishing the surface, every action is designed to feel fluid and immersive.

The Restoration Process

Here’s how you’ll go from rust bucket to showroom-ready:

Sanding Down the Rust: Start by grabbing sandpaper and removing the rust by moving your mouse left and right. You’ll need a few solid passes to remove the rust and prep the surface.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/458f7a9368a4e0312f4ca51361fe0b094baaf2f6.gif

Applying Putty: After cleaning, you’ll apply putty using a spatula. With each pass, you’ll spread the putty evenly across the surface, filling in any gaps and ensuring the area is smooth.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/82a2444afe8138d41bae12d64ce0bda654d0f3e1.gif

3. Sanding Again: Finally, you’ll make a second pass with the sandpaper to smooth out the putty and create a flawless surface ready for painting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/fecdbfcb5e879f1992ea96ad56f5f714ed5c21aa.gif

4. Painting: Choose your paint color, then spray it onto the prepared surface. Watch as the car is transformed from a rusty mess to a polished beauty, one layer at a time.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/7610a1424090dfec9c1234665c8b3bee54971b64.gif

Real-Time Progress and Feedback

You’ll see your progress reflected on the screen as you move through each step. A progress bar in the top-left corner will keep you updated, and helpful instructions will guide you along the way. If you’re unsure of what areas still need work, using radar will highlight unfinished spots, ensuring nothing gets left behind.

Bring Life Back to Every Car

With these bodywork mechanics, you’ll experience the satisfaction of turning worn-out, rusty cars into beautifully restored machines. Every sanding stroke, every layer of paint—it all adds up to the thrill of seeing a car shine like new.
Get ready to roll up your sleeves and dive into some serious restoration work. There’s nothing quite like the feeling of bringing a car back from the brink!

Hello Dealers,

We’re excited to share an update on Car Dealer Simulator as we continue to improve the game ahead of its release. Today, we want to talk about something you’ve often asked about—our car-driving mechanics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/88148bb99d88b8e1030b77b4eb0b6a66c0be7021.gif

Driving Mechanics Overview

As a car dealer, you won’t just be managing your dealership; you’ll also get behind the wheel to test-drive the cars yourself. To make sure this aspect of the game feels right, we’ve integrated the Chaos Vehicles System from Unreal Engine 5. This system brings a solid and responsive driving experience, ensuring that every car you test-drive feels distinct.

Key Features

Here are some of the highlights of what we’ve been working on:

Physics-Based Driving: The Chaos Vehicles System allows for more realistic vehicle physics. While it’s not a hardcore simulation, you’ll notice the weight and handling of each car as you drive. It’s balanced to be accessible and authentic, giving you a good sense of how each vehicle performs.

Responsive Handling: We’ve worked hard to make the driving controls responsive and intuitive. The handling should feel natural and satisfying, whether you’re taking a leisurely drive or pushing a car to see what it can do.

Different Experience for Different Cars: Many of you wanted to know if there will be multiple car models and types. Of course! More than that, we are doing our best to make the driving experience of each car model a bit different. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/5028d3f83002a9860a70275cd9a2049a666fd580.gif

What’s yet to be done?

Here are some of the things from our current TODO list:

Visual and Feedback Improvements: Our HUD is not final yet, so we are working on developing the right one – simple yet useful. We would also like to add visual touches that enhance the driving experience, like suspension movement and tire reactions. These details are subtle but help make the driver feel more grounded.

Customizable Controls: We know players have different preferences, so we’ve included options to adjust the driving controls to your liking. You can tweak the settings to find a balance that feels right. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/09c0e53d9a8d8b8112c820440c8d0a559253e126.gif

Preparing for Launch

As we approach release, we focus on refining these mechanics further. Our goal is to deliver a driving experience that complements the business management side of the game without overwhelming it. We want testing cars to be fun and an integral part of running your dealership.

Stay Tuned

We can’t wait for you to try these features for yourself when the game launches. In the meantime, we’ll continue to share updates on our progress. Your support means a lot to us as we work towards bringing Car Dealer Simulator to life.
